design_rationale:
[1 WHY A GOOD TEST] The caller (durable POA daughter) asks only to put her mother's Personal Services Companion Package on hold "for as long as it allows, starting as soon as possible". The scored figure is the number of whole months (3) the hold may run, which the published suspension rule builds from five inputs (package allowance, absence extension, time-in-force extension, past-due deduction, counting of the previous suspension). One of those inputs, the past-due amount, is a ledger reconciliation that is wrong until an overbilled visit is credited, and the suspension rule says outright that its result waits on that state. The agent must therefore (a) read the prerequisite sentence, (b) find in the ledger and the order records that the 2026-09-21 hourly charge (88.00 for 2.00 hours) belongs to a Saturday companion visit whose completion record shows 70 of 120 booked minutes, (c) re-rate that visit through six factors to a credit of 87.50 and post it, and only then (d) count the months. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling history and arithmetic, never from tool choice: two hidden tools, each named by exactly one policy.
[2 SCOPE SNAPSHOT] Claimed by task 0: services_ext_suspension_months (root, user tool sign_services_suspension_89d6021d) and services_ext_short_visit_credit (prerequisite, agent tool post_services_visit_credit_5ef485c2). Base subjects used: services_suspend, services_credit. Reserved for task 1 (draw: 1 prerequisite, factor counts [4,5]): a package change fitted to the resident's use (services_package_change_request, user tool) whose usage input waits on the hours owed for a late-cancelled or missed visit (services_hours_draw, agent tool) - different subjects, different tools, different factor families (late-cancellation notice bands, courtesy waivers; usage windows), so task 1 keeps an independent load-bearing tree. No task 0 asset is reused there.
[3 DRAW] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[6, 4]. services_ext_short_visit_credit takes 6 factors, services_ext_suspension_months takes 4. Tree size 1 prerequisite problem; value_input edges required max(1-1,1)=1 -> the single edge is value_input.
[4 PROBLEM-TREE CARD] root services_ext_suspension_months <- services_ext_short_visit_credit. kind value_input, gate binding past_due, form state. Prerequisite sentence (own rule of the root): "The number of months a suspension may run is fixed only after every hourly charge on the plan that its visit record shows billed on more time than was delivered carries a service dispute credit referencing it." Four-point test: (1) ordering connective "only after", affirmative direction (a figure 'is fixed only after' what it rests on, the way the desk states a computed allowance); (2) XX is a record-visible state (a service dispute credit entry referencing the charge), no action or performer named; (3) no tool, policy id or code token; (4) strength 'only after', scope 'every hourly charge ... billed on more time than was delivered' - exactly the condition field. Exactly one write of this difficulty books a service dispute credit referencing an overbilled hourly charge: the short-visit credit policy ("The correction is posted as one service dispute credit referencing that hourly charge"). Derivation: sentence + ledger (2026-09-21 hourly charge 88.00, 2.00 hours, order SO-2609-0389) + orders (SO-2609-0389 booked 2.00 h, completed 70 minutes) + the credit policy's rule -> the one resolving action is posting that credit. Why false at the opening: initial_state.services_ledger.<2026-09-21 charge>.amount=88.0, hours=2.0; initial_state.services_orders.<SO-2609-0389 completion>.actual_minutes=70; no services_credit references the charge. Resolving tool owner agent; root tool owner user (the caller signs as durable POA). Topological order: credit (step 9) then suspension (step 11). Deletion sensitivity (actual run): skipping the credit -> past_due 162.10 -> deduction 2 -> suspended_months 3 instead of 4; terminal ledger lacks the 87.50 credit. user_scenario never names the visit, the charge, a credit or a dispute; tools validate nothing (sign tool only updates suspension dates; credit tool only books what it is given).
[5 BASE-INVARIANT CARD] Step 9 subject services_credit: governing base policies services_cancellation_and_end (its gate residency_end_on_record applies to services_end only -> policy_scope; the credit is not a residency-end proration, the residency continues) and services_disputes_and_corrections: within_dispute_window (time; anchor services_ledger.posting_date of the disputed entry 2026-09-21, dispute_window_days 60, day 0 = posting date, inclusive -> last day 2026-11-20; frozen 2026-10-05 is day 14; negative case 2026-11-21 out of time) and one_correction_per_entry (dedup on source_entry_id + credit_reason: the only existing credit references the July charge, the only restore references the duplicate linen draw; nothing references the 2026-09-21 charge). Step 11 subject services_suspend: services_suspension: suspension_notice (time; anchor = first suspended month 2026-11-01, suspension_notice_days 7 from the variant, counted back in calendar days inclusive -> last request day 2026-10-25; 2026-10-05 qualifies; 2026-10-01 already begun so October cannot be suspended) and suspension_quota, which the extended policy retires by overwrite (its quota sentence is replaced by the allowance rule). The base rule text also requires an absence of at least suspension_min_absence_days (14): the assisted residency records the absence from 2026-09-24 and the caller confirms "well over that". Signer: the caller is the representative on file with representative_authority durable_poa, which services_enrollment_eligibility names as entitled to sign.
[6 BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD] Target of step 9: hourly charge entry of 2026-09-21 (order_reference SO-2609-0389, billing_period 2026-09, 88.00 / 2.00 h); correlation key = its services_entry_id, carried as source_entry_id of the credit. Rows that enter: the order's book row (2.00 h, Saturday 2026-09-19 13:00), its completion (70 minutes), its draw (0.50 h, 2026-09-21), the September month_end expiry (0.25 h), the 2026-08-03 service dispute credit (goodwill count). Rows excluded: the July hourly charge (already credited 2026-08-03, not the most recent), the 2026-09-17 a la carte transport charge (not an hourly charge), all draws of other orders. Target of step 11: the plan itself (services_plan_id), with its recorded suspension 2026-03-01..2026-04-30 overwritten by the new one.
[7 FACTOR CARD - services_ext_short_visit_credit (6)] delivered_time_billing (method; short visit -> round down; tier taken: 70 < 120 minutes -> 60 min = 1.00 h; baseline round up 75 min -> credit 77.00; near-miss: an agent that rounds up as base does gets 1.25 h). date_surcharge (parameter; 2026-09-19 is a Saturday, DAYS from 2026-01-03 mod 7 = 0, not in holiday_calendar -> 25%; baseline 0 -> credit capped 88.00). illness_relief (parameter, multi-source: the visit ended short (order record) and an absence is recorded (assisted residency); cross-difficulty assisted; rehab_facility absence from 2026-09-24 = 5 days after a visit cut short at 70 of 120 minutes -> x0.8; baseline x1 -> 77.00; near-miss: the absence is 5 days later, not within 3, so x0.5 does not apply). covering_hours_rule (method; September ended with a 0.25 h month_end expiry -> covering 0.50 + 0.25 = 0.75; baseline drawn only -> 77.00; the 2026-09-23 restore is NOT added because the expiry tier precedes it). entrance_overage_rate (parameter, cross-difficulty entrance; occupied LifeChoice 50% Refundable Plan, contract_type fee_for_service -> 42.00; baseline 44.00 -> 87.00). dispute_goodwill (parameter; one service dispute credit in 12 months (2026-08-03) -> 10.00; baseline 0 -> 77.50). All-baseline fall-back 55.00 (round up 1.25 h, no surcharge, no relief, 0.50 covering, 0.75 h x 44.00 = 33.00, 88.00-33.00). Expected 87.50.
[8 FACTOR CARD - services_ext_suspension_months (4)] Baseline (computation document): one total = max_suspension_months_per_12m 2 (starting allowance, not a ceiling) + time-in-force months (standard ladder on whole months since the effective date: >= 48 -> 2, >= 24 -> 1) - months of the most recent suspension that ended within the 12-month look-back, floored at zero once at the end. Factors: medical_absence_extension (parameter, cross-difficulty assisted; on_leave + rehab_facility -> +2; baseline 2). time_in_force_count (method: from the earlier independent living move-in for a resident admitted from Larkspur independent living / effective date less the suspended months for a plan with a recorded suspension / effective date; multi-source assisted admission_source + independent move_in_date; tier taken: 85 months from 2019-09-03 -> +2; baseline 31 months -> +1 -> 3). account_standing_deduction (parameter; 74.60 past due after the credit -> -1; baseline 5). previous_suspension_share (parameter; suspension ended 5 whole months ago, not within the absence -> share 0.5 -> 1 counted; baseline share 1 -> 3). Result 2+2+2-1-1 = 4. All-baseline fall-back 1 (2 + 1 - 2).
[9 OVERWRITE LEDGER] Credit policy supersedes four base clauses of services_hours_and_billing / services_disputes_and_corrections (rounding, hours drawn from availability, rate of the remainder, 'a draw or charge that matches ... is not an error', 'an upheld dispute ... is credited as service_dispute') each replaced by the quoted extended sentence; everything else (dispute window, one correction per entry, credit never above the disputed entry, charge on the same order) is inherited. Suspension policy supersedes the base quota sentence of services_suspension; notice, whole months, 14-day absence, fee/hours behaviour during suspension are inherited.
[10 WORLD ROWS] customers (identity + POA), assisted residency (on_leave, rehab, 2026-09-24, admitted from Larkspur independent living: relief + extension + time-in-force method), entrance agreement (occupied, fee-for-service: rate), closed independent residency (FK of the agreement; moved in 2019-09-03, the anchor of the time-in-force count; transfer_assisted 2024-02-12), plan (Companion, assisted, effective 2024-03-01, last suspension Mar-Apr 2026, caches 8.00 h / 521.10 equal to the ledger sums), 33 ledger rows July-October 2026 (fees, grants, draws, two hourly charges, one credit, one restore of a duplicate draw, two month-end expiries, a la carte transport 74.10, three autopays), 33 order rows (book/complete/cancel). Removing the expiry changes covering hours; removing the August credit drops goodwill; removing the rehab absence drops relief and the extension; removing the agreement drops the rate reduction. Automatic clauses checked: every month shows fee+grant on the 1st, August/September month-end expiries match the remaining hours, the July hours were exhausted (no expiry row), no rollover (Companion), the September statement is past due but its grace runs to 2026-10-11 so no late fee is owed at frozen_time, no returned payment.
[11 PERSONA] Karen Whitfield-Ames, tired but organised; volunteers only the hold request; identity on request (1937-11-03, 8724, phones); passive branches: correction needed -> 'go ahead'; months stated -> accepts; tool handed -> signs with the agent's values; confirmation -> ends. She never names any visit or charge. Asked about the account she only says September extras are unpaid and a check will be mailed (true in the ledger), asking nothing.
[12 STANDARD SOLUTION] find_customers(name) -> verify (DOB + SSN4) -> find_services_plans -> find_services_ledger -> find_services_orders -> find_assisted_residencies -> find_entrance_agreements -> find_independent_residencies -> unlock + call post_services_visit_credit_5ef485c2(plan, 2026-09-21 charge, service_dispute, 2026-09, 87.50) -> unlock_user + call_user sign_services_suspension_89d6021d(plan, 2026-11-01, 4).
[13 VERIFICATION RUN] .venv/bin/python /tmp/psp/sens.py 0 (handling-time replay through the real tools; temporary, removed at the end): credit result 87.5; factor baselines 77.0/88.0/77.0/77.0/87.0/77.5; all-baseline 55.0; suspension result 3; factor baselines 1/2/4/2 (round 3: 1/2/1/4 with time_in_force_count); all-baseline 0; skipping the credit -> 2. Gates: check_compute --task 0 COMPUTE OK; check_extended EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks REPLAY OK (71/71 closure); check_solvability SOLVABILITY OK; check_grounding GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire SCOPE OK.
[14 DRAFT RECOMPUTE FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT] Masking compute/expected: the suspension document (baseline) says allowance less counted months; the KB factor documents found from the records (on-leave rehab absence, admission from Larkspur independent living with an 85-month count from 2019-09-03, past-due balance, a suspension ended 5 months ago) give +2, +2, -?, -2; the prerequisite sentence sends the reader to the overbilled visit; the credit documents give 87.50 from the order and ledger figures; with the credit the past due is 74.60 -> -1 -> 4 months from 2026-11-01 (one total floored once). Same writes and values as gold; no second reading found (the restore tier is excluded because the expiry tier applies first; the July charge is already credited).
[15 REVISIONS] r1: account standing first read the cached account_balance -> check_extended requires record-derived evidence -> switched to a ledger reconciliation (SUM of charges less payments and credits). r2: a module-level date helper in task_tools.py was flagged as an undiscoverable tool -> inlined into the tool body; gates re-run green.

[16 ROUND-2 REWORK (audit policy_task/personal_services_packages)] F-1: previous_suspension_count is now a genuine method factor - its tiers select the look-back window (excluded / 6-month look-back for a suspension that ended 3 to 12 months ago / standard 12-month look-back), counted as MN(months, window - months since end); result unchanged (3), baseline 2, all-baseline 0. O-2: the past-due amount now subtracts the package fee row charged on the ledger for the current month (LATEST fee row whose posting month is the request month, nothing otherwise) instead of the tariff; same 74.60 on this world. O-1: the credit is 0 when the re-rated charge is not below the posted charge (rule sentence added); unchanged 87.50 here. O-6: illness relief now requires the visit to have ended short of its booked time (cut short by the illness that led to the admission); the visit delivered 70 of 120 minutes, so the tier and 87.50 stand. Whole-month and look-back conventions are stated in each rule (same day of a later month). Factor-trace labels corrected: medical_absence_extension and entrance_overage_rate are single-record factors (multi-source in this task: illness_relief, delivered_time_billing, previous_suspension_count). Sensitivity re-run: credit 87.5 / 77.0 / 88.0 / 77.0 / 77.0 / 87.0 / 77.5, all 55.0; suspension 3 / 1 / 2 / 4 / 2, all 0, skip credit 2.
[17 ROUND-3 REWORK] F-1 (not closed in round 2: a window change is still one method): previous_suspension_count is removed as a factor - the previous suspension is now plain plumbing with the standard 12-month look-back (counts 2). The method factor of the suspension computation is now time_in_force_count, whose tiers select different records and different rules: (a) months since the move-in date of the earlier Larkspur independent living residency (a different anchor record, read across categories); (b) months since the plan's effective date less the months of its recorded suspension (a subtraction of another quantity); (c) months since the effective date. The tenure ladder (time_in_force_extension) stays a parameter factor on the counted months. Task 0 values unchanged: credit 87.50, suspension 3 months; sensitivity 1 / 2 / 1 / 4, all-baseline 0, skip credit 2. O-8: the past-due rule now names the fee charged on the first day of the current month; the charter charges every package fee (including a package-change fee) on the first day of a month, so a mid-month fee row cannot occur and the latest-fee-row read is exact. O-5 and O-9: answered in the worklog (no change).
[18 ROUND-4 REWORK (render-layer audits policy_kb / runtime_context)] B1/N1: the suspension total is one sentence in both rule and baseline, floored once at the end ('never to a part of it'); the partial floor is gone. B2/E1/N2: time in force is now part of the baseline itself (standard ladder on whole months since the effective date), so the baseline carries no factor-only default and no 'as the standard' wording; the method factor time_in_force_count changes how the whole months are counted; the previous suspension's months become a parameter factor (share 0 / 0.5 / 1) on the baseline's 12-month count. Values: suspension 4 months (was 3) -> 2026-11-01..2027-02-28; sensitivity 2 / 3 / 5 / 3; all-baseline 1; skip credit 3. Credit unchanged 87.50. N3: the baseline says max_suspension_months_per_12m is the starting allowance, not a ceiling. N4: the three services_hours_and_billing overwrites (rounding, drawing, rest charged) are withdrawn so those rules stay in force for first postings; the credit rule states that its re-rating applies only to working out a correction, declared against the disputes clause 'a draw or charge that matches ... is not an error'. N5: lifecare / fee-for-service contracts are named by plan (LifeCare Declining Balance / LifeCare 90% Refundable; any LifeChoice plan).
user_scenario: You are Karen Whitfield-Ames, calling Larkspur's Resident and Family Services desk from your home in Austin about your mother, Eleanor Whitfield, who lives in assisted living at Larkspur at Willow Creek in Plano. You hold your mother's durable power of attorney and you handle her bills; you are organized, a little tired, and you speak plainly. Your mother went into the hospital in late September and has been in a rehabilitation facility since; once she is discharged she is coming to stay with you in Austin through the winter, so she will not be using her personal services package for months. What you want today is simple: put her personal services package on hold starting as soon as Larkspur allows, and for as long as her package allows. You have no particular months in mind and you do not know the package rules; you will take whatever the longest hold is. You expect to sign the hold yourself as her agent if the desk sends it to you. Open by saying who you are, that you are calling for your mother Eleanor Whitfield, and that you would like to put her personal services package on hold for as long as it allows, starting as soon as possible. You give identifying details only when the agent asks for them: your mother's full name is Eleanor Whitfield, her date of birth is 1937-11-03, and the last four digits of her Social Security number are 8724; if a phone number is asked for, hers is 4695550142 and yours is 4695550167. If the agent asks whether she will be away for at least two weeks, you say yes, well over that. If asked when she will be back, you say sometime in the spring, you are not sure exactly. If the agent asks about her account, you say you know a few extra charges from her September statement are still unpaid and you were planning to mail a check next week; you do not want to make a payment on this call. If the agent tells you something on her account has to be corrected or credited before the hold can be worked out, you say that is fine, please go ahead, and you wait; you have no idea what it might be and you do not ask for details beyond what the agent offers. When the agent tells you how many months the hold will run and from which month, you accept it as the maximum. When the agent hands you the hold to sign, you sign it with exactly the plan, the first month and the number of months the agent gives you, and you read back the dates the confirmation shows. Once the agent confirms the hold is recorded, you thank them and end the call. You never suggest how the hold should be calculated, you never name any charge or visit on her account, and if the agent says something you do not understand you simply ask them to put it in plain words.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.services_plan_id: df70605f-04c3-4f42-9b1d-889d1b3aeb30 — basis: the Id-class contract of the credit tool ('the reference number of the personal services plan whose account is credited, as returned by the personal services plan lookup') and the find_services_plans return for customer 7fa85340-bdaa-4db8-8d81-ce0b4145edf5; uniqueness: the customer holds exactly one plan, the Personal Services Companion Package, so no other plan reference exists.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_entry_id: 0cf232c7-66ac-4b99-98ba-3eb66cdc9088 — basis: services_ext_short_visit_credit rule 'corrections are made one charge at a time beginning with the most recently posted hourly charge for a delivered visit' and 'The correction is posted as one service dispute credit referencing that hourly charge'; the ledger read shows the hourly charges for delivered visits are the 2026-07-29 charge (already credited on 2026-08-03) and the 2026-09-21 charge of 88.00 on order SO-2609-0389, entry 0cf232c7-66ac-4b99-98ba-3eb66cdc9088; uniqueness: it is the most recently posted such charge and no credit references it, so it is the only entry the rule selects.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.credit_reason: service_dispute — basis: the rule sentence 'The correction is posted as one service dispute credit referencing that hourly charge' and the docstring value 'service_dispute when a charge is corrected because the service was not delivered, was delivered short, or was billed twice'; uniqueness: billing_error is for a charge 'posted against the wrong plan or at the wrong rate' (the charge was on the right plan at the package rate) and residency_end_proration is for a residency's end (the residency continues), so neither applies.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.billing_period: 2026-09 — basis: the rule sentence 'carrying the billing month of the charge' and the docstring 'the month of the charge being credited'; the 2026-09-21 hourly charge carries billing_period 2026-09; uniqueness: it is copied from the credited entry, no other month is related to it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 87.50 — calculated by services_ext_short_visit_credit on the world after identity verification: the 2026-09-21 hourly charge 88.00 on SO-2609-0389; delivered 70 of 120 booked minutes -> rounded down to 60 minutes = 1.00 hour (companion minimum 1.0 not binding); Saturday 2026-09-19 -> weekend surcharge 25% = 1.25; rehab absence recorded from 2026-09-24, 5 days after the visit -> x0.8 = 1.00 billable hours; hours covering the visit = 0.50 drawn on the order + 0.25 expired at the September month end = 0.75; re-rated hours 0.25 at 44.00 - 2.00 (occupied LifeChoice 50% Refundable Plan, a fee-for-service contract) = 42.00 -> 10.50; difference 77.50 plus goodwill 10.00 for one service dispute credit in the last 12 months (2026-08-03) = 87.50, below the 88.00 cap.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.services_plan_id: df70605f-04c3-4f42-9b1d-889d1b3aeb30 — basis: the Id-class contract of the suspension tool ('the reference number of the personal services plan being suspended, as returned by the personal services plan lookup') and the find_services_plans return; uniqueness: the resident holds one plan.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.first_suspended_month: 2026-11-01 — basis: services_ext_suspension_months rule 'from the first calendar month whose first day is at least suspension_notice_days days after the request is signed' with suspension_notice_days 7 for the Companion Package and the caller's 'starting as soon as possible'; the request is signed 2026-10-05, 2026-10-01 has passed and 2026-11-01 is 27 days ahead (the last day to request a November start is 2026-10-25); uniqueness: October is already running and any later month is not 'as soon as possible'.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.suspended_months: 4 — calculated by services_ext_suspension_months on the world after the credit at step 9, as one total floored at zero only at the end: max_suspension_months_per_12m 2 (Companion Package, the starting allowance) + 2 months for an assisted living residency on leave for a rehabilitation absence + 2 months for time in force (the resident came to assisted living from Larkspur independent living, so the whole months run from the 2019-09-03 independent move-in: 85, at least 48) - 1 month for a ledger past-due amount of 74.60 (433.60 owed after the 87.50 credit, less the 359.00 fee charged on 2026-10-01) - 1 month for the 2026-03-01 to 2026-04-30 suspension (both months ended fewer than 12 whole months before the request, and it ended 5 whole months before, at least 3, so it counts at half: 2 x 0.5 = 1) = 4.

edges.condition: Every services_hourly_charge on the plan whose order's completion record shows fewer delivered minutes than the time billed has a services_credit with credit_reason service_dispute whose source_entry_id is that charge, so the balance the ledger shows owed no longer includes the overbilled amount.
edges.policy_source: The number of months a suspension may run is fixed only after every hourly charge on the plan that its visit record shows billed on more time than was delivered carries a service dispute credit referencing it.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The 2026-09-21 hourly charge of 88.00 billed 2.00 hours on order SO-2609-0389 whose completion record shows 70 of 120 booked minutes delivered, and no ledger entry references it as a credit.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The step-9 credit of 87.50 with credit_reason service_dispute and source_entry_id = the 2026-09-21 charge lands; the ledger balance owed falls from 521.10 to 433.60 and the past-due amount from 162.10 to 74.60, moving the account standing deduction from 2 months to 1 and the suspension from 3 months to 4.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge, no parallel prerequisites: the credit must land before the suspension count because the count reads the ledger balance the credit changes; the reverse order gives 3 months instead of 4 (verified by the sensitivity run).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the credit leaves past_due at 162.10 (>= 100.00), the standing deduction at 2 and suspended_months = 3 instead of 4; the terminal ledger also lacks the 87.50 credit and the plan balance stays 521.10 instead of 433.60.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only for a hold of the package 'for as long as it allows'; it never names the 19 September visit, a short visit, an overcharge, a credit or a dispute, and it states the instruction to stay silent on any charge or visit. The only account statement it contains (unpaid September extras, planned check) is given solely on the agent's question and names no error; when the agent says a correction is needed the caller merely consents.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: sign_services_suspension_89d6021d performs one ctx.update of suspension_start_date / suspension_end_date with the months passed and never reads the ledger, the credits or the balance; it records 2 months as faithfully as 3 and returns no error or hint when the credit is missing. post_services_visit_credit_5ef485c2 likewise writes whatever amount it is given.

factor_trace: delivered_time_billing (method): order SO-2609-0389 booked 2.00 hours (120 minutes), completion record 70 minutes delivered -> fewer minutes delivered than booked -> rounded down to whole 15-minute increments = 60 minutes = 1.00 hour; the baseline (round up to the next increment) gives 75 minutes = 1.25 hours and a credit of 77.00.

date_surcharge (parameter): visit date 2026-09-19 is a Saturday not in holiday_calendar (DAYS from 2026-01-03 mod 7 = 0) -> weekend_surcharge_pct 25 of the Companion Package; the baseline (no surcharge) gives billable hours 0.80 and a credit capped at the 88.00 charge.

illness_relief (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty assisted): the visit ended short of its booked time (70 of 120 minutes, order SO-2609-0389) and the assisted residency records a rehab_facility absence starting 2026-09-24, 5 days after the visit -> more than relief_short_days 3 and at most relief_long_days 7 -> multiplier relief_long_factor 0.8; the baseline (no multiplier) leaves 1.25 billable hours and a credit of 77.00.

covering_hours_rule (method): month 2026-09 ended with a 0.25-hour month_end expiry -> hours covering the visit = 0.50 drawn on the order + 0.25 expired = 0.75; the baseline (only the 0.50 drawn) gives a credit of 77.00.

entrance_overage_rate (parameter, cross-difficulty entrance): occupied Entrance Fee Agreement on the LifeChoice 50% Refundable Plan, contract_type fee_for_service -> 44.00 - 2.00 = 42.00 per hour; the baseline 44.00 gives a credit of 87.00.
dispute_goodwill (parameter): one service dispute credit posted in the last 12 months (2026-08-03, 44.00 for order SO-2607-0677) -> goodwill_one 10.00; the baseline 0 gives a credit of 77.50.

plumbing: visit_ref = SO-2609-0389 (latest hourly charge for a delivered visit, posted 2026-09-21); charged_amount = 88.00; visit_month = 2026-09; floor_hours = companion_visit_minimum_hours 1.0 (not binding); base_hours = 1.00; billable_hours = RND(1.00 x 1.25 x 0.8, 2) = 1.00; rerated_hours = 1.00 - 0.75 = 0.25; rerated_charge = 0.25 x 42.00 = 10.50; result = MN(88.00, 88.00 - 10.50 + 10.00) = 87.50 (the re-rated charge 10.50 is below the posted 88.00, so the charge was billed on more time than the visit supports).

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: fewer minutes were delivered than the order booked
the visit date is a Saturday or Sunday not in holiday_calendar

the visit ended short of its booked time and the assisted living residency records a hospital or rehabilitation absence that began more than relief_short_days and at most relief_long_days days after the visit date
hours expired unused at the end of the visit's billing month
the resident holds an occupied Entrance Fee Agreement and its plan is a fee-for-service contract
exactly one service dispute credit was posted on the plan in the last dispute_lookback_months months

factor_trace: medical_absence_extension (parameter, cross-difficulty assisted): assisted residency status on_leave and absence_reason rehab_facility -> medical_extra_on_leave 2 months; the baseline (no month added) gives 2.

time_in_force_count (method, multi-source, cross-difficulty independent/assisted): the assisted residency records admission_source larkspur_independent and the earlier independent living residency records move_in_date 2019-09-03 -> the whole months run from that move-in: 85 -> at least 48 -> time in force adds 2; the baseline method (whole months since the plan's effective date 2024-03-01 = 31 -> adds 1) gives 3.

account_standing_deduction (parameter): ledger charges 1642.10 less payments 1077.00 and credits 44.00 + 87.50 (the prerequisite credit) = 433.60, less the package fee charged on the first day of the current month (359.00, 2026-10-01) = 74.60 past due -> above zero and below 100.00 -> 1 month deducted; the baseline (no deduction) gives 5; without the prerequisite credit the past due is 162.10 -> 2 months deducted -> result 3.

previous_suspension_share (parameter, cross-difficulty assisted): the most recent recorded suspension 2026-03-01..2026-04-30 did not lie within the recorded absence (which began 2026-09-24) and ended MONTHS(2026-04-30, 2026-10-05) = 5 whole months before the request, at least 3 -> share 0.5; months counted in the 12-month look-back 2 -> int(2 x 0.5) = 1; the baseline (share 1) counts 2 and gives 3.
plumbing: max_base = 2 (Companion); time-in-force months converted by the standard ladder (>= 48 -> 2, >= 24 -> 1); result = MX(0, 2 + 2 + 2 - 1 - 1) = 4, the floor applied once to the total.

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: the assisted living residency is on leave and its recorded absence is a hospital or rehabilitation absence
the resident came to the assisted living residency the plan serves from a Larkspur independent living residency whose move-in date is on record
the ledger balance owed less the current month's package fee is above zero and below high_past_due
it did not, and it ended at least older_suspension_months whole months before the request
